patch.sql:
with source_data as (
    select
        o_orderkey as order_key,
        o_custkey as customer_key,
        o_orderstatus as order_status,
        o_totalprice as total_price,
        o_orderdate as order_date,
        o_orderpriority as priority,
        _loaded_at as loaded_at
    from {{ source('raw', 'orders') }}
),
-- Keep only the first occurrence of each order_key. Duplicates are exact copies, so any row is fine.
deduped as (
    select
        order_key,
        customer_key,
        order_status,
        total_price,
        order_date,
        priority,
        loaded_at,
        row_number() over (partition by order_key order by loaded_at) as rn
    from source_data
)
select
    order_key,
    customer_key,
    order_status,
    total_price,
    order_date,
    priority,
    loaded_at
from deduped
where rn = 1
patch.explanation: Added a CTE to read from the raw orders source, then applied row_number partitioned by order_key to drop exact duplicate rows. Since duplicates are identical, keeping the first (earliest loaded_at) satisfies the unique constraint without altering column names or types.
